title: Rigorix Compaction Checkpoint v1
description: ADR-016 anchor-signed compaction checkpoint: the proof that a contiguous range of a producer's chain was deliberately erased (GDPR / retention). A verifier accepts a chain gap IF AND ONLY IF it is covered by a checkpoint whose `prior_head`/`new_head` are the hashes bracketing the gap and whose `sequence_from..sequence_to` is exactly the missing range; an uncovered gap is a failure. Deletion becomes a recorded, provable compaction rather than a silent absence.

prior_head.description: `envelope_hash` of the envelope immediately BEFORE the erased range — the hash the first erased successor would have stored in `prev_hash`.

new_head.description: `envelope_hash` of the envelope immediately AFTER the erased range. The successor after the gap stores this as its `prev_hash`, linking across the gap.

sig.description: Ed25519 signature (hex, 64 bytes) over the canonical checkpoint bytes (`sig` set to null).

x-signing.canonicalization: serde_json::to_string(checkpoint with `sig` = null) — UTF-8 bytes; no map fields.
x-signing.publicKey: 32-byte Ed25519 public key, hex; supplied out-of-band.
